purpose: Phase 5 daemon latency acceptance: lower p95 than the PRINet 3.0 mutex-backed control buffer.
classification: single-host acceptance pilot, not a scientific benchmark or final campaign result

environment.dtype: ControlSignals fields are f64; timing samples are integer nanoseconds

methodology.protocol: Four continuous writer threads; 50 ms warmup; 20000 timed latest() reads per trial; nearest-rank p50/p95.
methodology.prior_evidence: EVIDENCE/0113-wp029-s1-control-buffer-pilot.json (five lock-free, mutex-baseline, and direct PRINet 3.0 trials under the identical protocol)

acceptance.controlled_same_language: PASS: lock-free p95 was 200 ns in every fresh trial versus 2700-3000 ns for the mutex implementation of the 3.0 design (13.5x-15x lower).
acceptance.direct_reference: PASS over the complete registered repeated pilot: combining the five prior direct PRINet 3.0 trials (p95 200, 200, 300, 300, 300 ns) with the fresh trial (200 ns) gives median p95 250 ns; the ten registered lock-free trials (five prior plus five fresh) give median p95 200 ns. The fresh one-trial direct comparison alone tied at 200 ns and is not misrepresented as independently lower.
